PAPERS.short: Papatheodorou prenatal wildfire PM2.5 ASD ADHD Medicaid 2026
PAPERS.title: Prenatal Exposure to Wildfire PM2.5 and Risk of ASD and ADHD in Children Enrolled in Medicaid
PAPERS.pm: Weekly wildfire-smoke-attributable PM2.5 (1 km), aggregated to residential ZIP code across pregnancy
PAPERS.endpoint: Incident ASD and ADHD (validated claims algorithms)
PAPERS.n: Nationwide Medicaid (MAX) cohort of 893,212 mother-child pairs with stable ZIP code in pregnancy; 8,357 ASD and 22,302 ADHD diagnoses (cumulative incidence to age 8: 1.9% and 10.4%). Cox models with distributed-lag nonlinear terms. Per IQR (0.75 ug/m3) of cumulative smoke PM2.5: ASD HR 1.30 (1.07-1.59); ADHD HR 1.03 (0.91-1.17). The ASD window sat in mid to late gestation. Limitation: a 30% hazard increase per 0.75 ug/m3 is very steep for a ZIP-level smoke fraction; smoke years and regions coincide with secular and regional shifts in ASD claims coding, and claims-based diagnosis in Medicaid depends on service access. Relevance: high - smoke-specific PM at sub-ug/m3 contrasts is exactly where dense sensor networks add resolution over 1 km model fields.

PAPERS.short: Pedersen early-life air pollution lung function COPSAC 2026
PAPERS.title: Impact of air pollution exposure in early life on lung function development in the COPSAC cohorts
PAPERS.pm: Modelled multi-source PM2.5 and NO2 at home address (DEHM/UBM/AirGIS-type chain)
PAPERS.endpoint: FEV1 and specific airway resistance (spirometry, plethysmography) age 3-18
PAPERS.n: Two Copenhagen birth cohorts (n=846) with repeated spirometry and plethysmography from age 3 to 18 years; linear mixed models. Per IQR (2.2 ug/m3) of postnatal PM2.5: FEV1 at age 6 -2.70% (-4.27 to -1.10) and specific airway resistance +7.30% (1.87-13.07). The deficit and the resistance increase persisted in growth trajectories through childhood, stronger in males. Limitation: COPSAC is an asthma-enriched cohort (COPSAC2000 enrolled children of asthmatic mothers), so effect sizes may not transfer to the general population; a 2.2 ug/m3 IQR in Copenhagen is small and partly a proxy for urban residence. Relevance: medium - effects at very low contrast argue for address-level precision rather than municipal means.

PAPERS.short: Zhou short-term indoor PM2.5 cognition HRV randomized crossover 2026
PAPERS.title: Short-term indoor fine particulate matter exposure impedes cognitive performance and autonomic nervous system in adults
PAPERS.pm: Candle-generated indoor PM2.5, 1.70 vs 31.22 ug/m3 (purifier vs sham filter)
PAPERS.endpoint: Cognitive tests (attention, memory, coordination, reasoning); HRV; electrodermal activity
PAPERS.n: Randomised single-blind crossover in 90 working-age adults, two stable chamber conditions set by an air purifier with real or sham filter: 1.70 vs 31.22 ug/m3 PM2.5 from candle burning. The high condition lowered heart rate variability and attention and memory scores, but not coordination or reasoning; reduced HRV partly mediated some cognitive declines. Effect sizes with CIs are not given in the abstract. Limitation: candle smoke carries VOCs, CO, odour and visible haze, so blinding and the PM-specific attribution are both weak; multiple cognitive domains invite selective significance. Relevance: medium - controlled indoor steps of this size are what consumer PM monitors can verify in occupied rooms.

PAPERS.short: Hoang PM2.5 minimal residual disease childhood ALL REDIAL 2026
PAPERS.title: Fine particulate matter and minimal residual disease in childhood acute lymphoblastic leukemia from the REDIAL consortium
PAPERS.pm: CDC daily census-tract PM2.5 during induction (residence; centre then residence)
PAPERS.endpoint: Positive end-of-induction MRD (>=0.1% or >=0.01%)
PAPERS.n: 2,125 children with ALL; mean daily residential PM2.5 during induction in quartiles; logistic regression. In B-ALL, positive end-of-induction MRD: Q2 aOR 1.56 (1.08-2.24), Q3 1.51 (1.05-2.17), Q4 1.19 (n.s.). Restricted to NCI high-risk B-ALL, aORs rose to 1.73-2.28 across Q2-Q4. Limitation: a non-monotone quartile pattern with the top quartile null is not a dose-response; census-tract PM2.5 over a ~4-week induction is tightly tied to treatment centre and ethnicity, which REDIAL was built to study and which also predicts MRD. Relevance: low-medium - induction-window exposure is short enough that a home monitor would be the right instrument.

PAPERS.short: Li ambient air pollution gastric cancer incidence 204 countries ecological 2026
PAPERS.title: Ambient Air Pollution and Gastric Cancer Incidence: A Multinational Ecological Analysis (1990-2020)
PAPERS.pm: GBD 2021 national population-weighted PM2.5, NO2, O3
PAPERS.endpoint: Age-standardised gastric cancer incidence
PAPERS.n: Negative-binomial fixed-effects panel over 204 countries, 1990-2020, from GBD 2021. Per unit PM2.5: +0.3% (0.1-0.5%) in age-standardised gastric cancer incidence; NO2 +1.8% (1.2-2.4%), O3 +0.6% (0.3-0.9%). Splines show nonlinearity; PM2.5 lag window 3-4 years; male and high-middle-SDI strata most affected. Limitation: both exposure and outcome are GBD modelled quantities that share covariates (SDI), and a 3-4 year lag for a cancer with a decades-long Helicobacter-driven course is biologically implausible; country fixed effects do not remove the H. pylori decline that tracks development. The authors concede ecological status and call for individual-level validation. Relevance: low.

PAPERS.short: Vikas wavelet background PM2.5 India MERRA-2 2026
PAPERS.title: Estimating background PM2.5 concentrations using a wavelet-based convolution framework
PAPERS.pm: MERRA-2 reanalysis PM2.5; CPCB monitors for evaluation
PAPERS.endpoint: Regional background PM2.5 field
PAPERS.n: Wavelet coherence of low-frequency components across neighbouring MERRA-2 cells yields a spatiotemporal PM2.5 background map for India, capturing the IGP winter build-up and pre-monsoon dust in the northwest. Against a GMM-HMM background at four cities, MAD 2.2 (Kolkata) to 10.8 (Delhi) ug/m3. Against 5th-percentile PCHIP backgrounds across the Delhi network, MAE 21.95 and RMSE 29.45 ug/m3, improving to 14.03/17.65 at the Delhi background site. Limitation: validation is against other statistical background definitions, not tracer or model source attribution, and MERRA-2 PM2.5 is a reconstructed aerosol product with known bias over South Asia. Relevance: high - background/increment separation is a standard post-processing step for dense LCS networks.

PAPERS.short: Kara Pythagorean fuzzy PM2.5 monitoring station placement Trabzon 2026
PAPERS.title: A Pythagorean Fuzzy decision making framework for PM2.5 monitoring station placement in urban areas: A case study of Trabzon, Turkiye
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 monitoring network siting (criteria-weighted)
PAPERS.endpoint: Ranking of candidate monitoring sites
PAPERS.n: Modified Delphi to set eight criteria, PF-SWARA to weight them and PF-CODAS to rank five candidate sites in Trabzon. PM2.5 level weighted highest, then population density and distance to existing stations; a shopping-mall site ranked first. Limitation: the criterion weights are expert judgment; there is no objective function (coverage, representativeness, variance reduction) and no test that the chosen site improves exposure estimation. Weighting 'PM2.5 concentration' highest is circular when the network is being sited to measure it, and five alternatives make the ranking near-trivial. Relevance: medium - a contrast case for data-driven siting (kriging variance, information gain) that LCS deployments use.

PAPERS.short: Liang deep learning low-visibility events fog-haze eastern China 2026
PAPERS.title: Classification and quantification of low-visibility events using deep learning over eastern China
PAPERS.pm: Surface PM2.5 with geostationary satellite and meteorology
PAPERS.endpoint: Low-visibility event class (fog, sea fog, fog-haze) and intensity
PAPERS.n: A unified CNN fuses geostationary imagery, meteorology and surface PM2.5 to map and classify low-visibility events, separating polluted fog-haze from clean fog over land and sea. Scenario analysis: a 20% cut in PM2.5 shrinks winter fog-haze area by 43% but population exposure to fog-haze only by 15%, because the most populated and most polluted regions coincide; >40% PM2.5 reduction is needed there. Limitation: the scenario perturbs PM2.5 as a model input, so it inherits the learned correlation rather than fog microphysics (hygroscopic growth, aerosol-fog feedback); classification skill metrics are not in the abstract. Relevance: medium - humidity-driven haze is the regime where optical LCS fail.

PAPERS.short: Cerin air pollution road environment cardiometabolic walking AusDiab 2026
PAPERS.title: Associations of Ambient Air Pollution and Road-Related Environmental Characteristics with Cardiometabolic Health: The Role of Walking
PAPERS.pm: Residential PM2.5 and NO2 (modelled); road density, distance to nearest busy road
PAPERS.endpoint: Blood pressure, lipids, HbA1c, waist; walking time
PAPERS.n: 4,141 middle-aged and older adults; GAMMs with FDR control within test families. PM2.5 associated positively with diastolic and non-linearly with systolic BP; road density with lower HDL and higher triglycerides. Higher PM2.5 and NO2 were associated with more walking for transport, setting up opposing pathways via physical activity. Coefficients are not reported in the abstract. Limitation: cross-sectional, so walking cannot be ordered between exposure and outcome, as the authors state; Australian PM2.5 contrasts are narrow (single-digit ug/m3) and track urbanity, which drives both walkability and pollution. Relevance: low-medium - co-located PM and mobility data would let LCS studies separate these pathways.

PAPERS.short: Ai air pollution IVF outcomes Chengdu retrospective cohort 2026
PAPERS.title: Association between Ambient Air Pollution Exposure and Reproductive Outcomes following In Vitro Fertilization: A Retrospective Cohort Study
PAPERS.pm: CHAP 1 km PM2.5, PM10, O3, NO2 at residence by IVF stage
PAPERS.endpoint: Biochemical pregnancy, clinical pregnancy, live birth after fresh embryo transfer
PAPERS.n: 12,453 women with fresh embryo transfer at one Chengdu centre, 2019-2022; exposure windows defined around oocyte retrieval and transfer; GLMs adjusted for clinical, sociodemographic and paternal factors. Exposure in the 85 days before oocyte retrieval (folliculogenesis window) was associated with lower odds of biochemical pregnancy, clinical pregnancy and live birth; live birth OR 0.969 (0.954-0.984) per 10 ug/m3 PM2.5. Limitation: four pollutants over several overlapping windows from 4 years of gridded data raise multiplicity, and in a single-city clinic cohort the exposure contrast is mostly temporal, confounded by season and protocol changes (including COVID-era disruption). Relevance: low.

PAPERS.journal: Am J Respir Crit Care Med
PAPERS.short: Zhou preoperative short-term PM2.5 postoperative pulmonary complications lung cancer surgery 2026
PAPERS.title: Preoperative short-term PM2.5 Exposure and Postoperative Pulmonary Complications After Lung Cancer Surgery
PAPERS.pm: Short-term preoperative PM2.5 (metadata only)
PAPERS.endpoint: Postoperative pulmonary complications after lung cancer resection
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: the record (AJRCCM research letter) carried no abstract at PubMed, Crossref or Semantic Scholar on the issue date. The title reports an association of short-term PM2.5 exposure before surgery with postoperative pulmonary complications after lung cancer resection; design, n and effect size are not available here and are not inferred. Limitation (structural): preoperative exposure windows are short, so day-of-week and seasonal surgical scheduling and hospital load are the confounders any such analysis has to defeat. Relevance: medium - a perioperative window is one where short-horizon PM forecasts could change clinical scheduling. Retry the abstract before the weekly.

PAPERS.short: Chen PM2.5 mitochondria-associated membranes mouse liver 2026
PAPERS.title: Exposure to airborne PM2.5 suppresses mitochondrial associated membranes and MAM-associated metabolic regulators in mouse liver
PAPERS.design: Animal exposure study + in vitro receptor overexpression
PAPERS.pm: Concentrated ambient PM2.5 inhalation (mouse); PM2.5 particles on hepatocytes/macrophages
PAPERS.endpoint: Hepatic MAM abundance, UPRmt and fatty-acid oxidation programs (CREBH/PPARalpha)
PAPERS.n: Mice inhaling environmentally relevant PM2.5 showed fewer mitochondria-associated membranes and fewer MAM-forming mitochondria in liver (TEM). In hepatocytes, PM2.5 suppressed basal and glucagon-induced MAM formation (BiFC sensor); macrophage particle uptake was blocked by antioxidants or calcium chelation. Mechanism: repression of CREBH/PPARalpha programs for the mitochondrial unfolded protein response and fatty-acid oxidation. Limitation: in vitro particle doses and the inhaled dose to liver are not reconciled, and the translocation route (systemic particles vs lung-derived mediators) is assumed rather than shown. Sample sizes are not in the abstract. Relevance: low - mechanism for PM-metabolic associations.

PAPERS.short: Qu PM2.5-bound heavy metals source apportionment Laibin winter 2026
PAPERS.title: Source Apportionment and Health Risk Assessment of PM2.5-Bound Heavy Metals in Wintertime Laibin, Guangxi, China
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 mass and nine metals (Zn, Cr, Ni, Pb, V, Cu, Sb, Cd, Co), day/night filters
PAPERS.endpoint: PMF sources; inhalation HI and carcinogenic risk
PAPERS.n: 42-day winter 2025 campaign: mean PM2.5 47.6 ug/m3, higher at night with lower wind and shallower boundary layer; nine metals summed 363.0 ng/m3, dominated by Zn, Cr and Ni, with severe Cd and significant Ni enrichment. PMF: non-ferrous smelting plus coal combustion 43%, industrial combustion 34%, traffic 23%; traffic share rose at night. Hazard index <1 for all groups; carcinogenic risk slightly above 1e-4 under winter scenarios, Cr dominant. Limitation: PMF on nine species and ~84 day/night samples is under-determined (the authors say 'preliminarily'), and Cr risk depends on an assumed Cr(VI) fraction. Relevance: low-medium - nocturnal boundary-layer peaks are visible to any LCS node.

PAPERS.short: Park PM2.5 composition sources COVID-19 social distancing Seoul 2026
PAPERS.title: Restructuring of PM2.5 Composition and Source Contributions Across COVID-19 Social Distancing Periods: A Case Study at an Urban Monitoring Site in Seoul, South Korea
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 mass and speciation, PMF (7 factors), GAM meteorological adjustment
PAPERS.endpoint: Source contributions pre-, during and post-distancing
PAPERS.n: Feb 2018-Mar 2024 at one Seoul site, split into pre-, during- and post-distancing periods; PMF with GAM adjustment for meteorology and season. PM2.5 stayed lower during and after distancing. Secondary inorganic aerosol remained dominant with no period effect after adjustment; metal industry fell then partly rebounded; construction dust stayed elevated and paved-road dust rose post-distancing. Limitation: one site, and 'post-distancing' is also the period of Korea's seasonal-management PM policy and Chinese emission reductions, so the periods confound policy and transboundary change with social activity. No effect sizes in the abstract. Relevance: medium - non-exhaust road dust is a coarse-mode source optical LCS undercount.

PAPERS.short: Somsunun PM2.5-bound metals health risk haze season Chiang Mai 2026
PAPERS.title: Health Risk Assessment of Ambient PM2.5-Bound Metals During Haze Seasons in Urban and Rural Chiang Mai, Thailand
PAPERS.pm: 24 h PM2.5 filters (n=101) and metals, three land-use sites
PAPERS.endpoint: Metal enrichment, inhalation HI and total cancer risk
PAPERS.n: 101 24 h samples, 15 Jan-22 Apr 2020 haze season, at urban (CMU), agricultural rural (Mae Chaem) and roadside rural (Chom Thong) sites. Median PM2.5 50.3, 42.1 and 64.9 ug/m3. Despite lower mass, Mae Chaem had HI 2.10 and TCR 2.37e-4 vs CMU 1.34 and 1.18e-4; HI >1 and TCR >1e-4 at all sites, highest at Chom Thong (2.69; 3.63e-4), driven by Cr. Limitation: risk is dominated by total Cr with an assumed Cr(VI) share, and spring 2020 overlaps COVID-19 restrictions. Relevance: medium - a direct case that equal PM2.5 mass from a sensor does not mean equal hazard across land uses.

PAPERS.short: Kwon seasonal PM2.5 secondary inorganic aerosol livestock rural Ulsan 2026
PAPERS.title: Seasonal Composition of PM2.5 and Secondary Inorganic Aerosols at a Rural Site near Livestock Facilities in Ulsan, South Korea
PAPERS.pm: Weekly 24 h PM2.5 filters, eight water-soluble ions
PAPERS.endpoint: Seasonal SIA composition, NH4+/SO4 2- ratios, neutralisation index
PAPERS.n: Weekly 24 h filters, June 2023-November 2025, at a rural site near livestock facilities. PM2.5 peaked in spring; nitrate peaked in winter and was lowest in summer (seasonal means 3.00 and 0.26 ug/m3). Elevated ammonium-to-sulfate ratios were frequent in spring and winter, but nitrate exceeded sulfate by mass far more often in winter, so the PM2.5 maximum and the nitrate maximum do not coincide. Limitation: one sample a week, no gas-phase NH3/HNO3 matched in time and no thermodynamic modelling, so ammonia-limited vs nitrate-limited regimes cannot be assigned, as the authors state. Relevance: low-medium - semi-volatile nitrate is a known source of LCS-vs-FEM divergence.

PAPERS.short: Zhao interpretable machine learning multi-window PM2.5 hypertension CHNS Beijing 2026
PAPERS.title: An Interpretable Machine Learning Framework Integrating Multi-Window Environmental Exposure for Hypertension Risk Assessment
PAPERS.pm: Cumulative PM2.5 over 0, 7, 15, 30 and 60 days
PAPERS.endpoint: Prevalent hypertension (classification)
PAPERS.n: Five classifiers (GLM, Lasso, tree, RF, XGBoost) with SHAP and partial-dependence layers on 2,523 participant-visits from the CHNS Beijing subsample; person-level and year-based splits; BP excluded from predictors. Test AUC 0.69-0.77, Brier 0.17-0.23. The 60-day PM2.5 window was the top exposure feature and added ~0.02-0.03 AUC (p=0.03-0.05). Adjusted window-specific analyses showed inverse PM2.5-hypertension associations, stronger for longer windows. Limitation: a ~0.02 AUC gain at borderline p with inverse associations indicates that the PM2.5 windows act as calendar/season proxies, not causal exposure; feature importance is not effect estimation, and the CHNS visit spacing is irregular. Relevance: low.

PAPERS.short: Chen PM2.5 mixtures Parkinson disease INPP5D SHIP1 PI3K-AKT multi-omics 2026
PAPERS.title: Neurotoxicity of PM2.5-Bound Multi-Pollutant Mixtures in Parkinson's Disease: Exploring the INPP5D/SHIP1-PI3K-AKT Axis via an Integrative Multi-Omics Study
PAPERS.pm: GWAS-instrumented PM2.5; NIST SRM 1648a urban PM in SH-SY5Y cells
PAPERS.endpoint: PD susceptibility; SHIP1/PI3K-AKT signalling, neuroinflammation, apoptosis
PAPERS.n: Two-sample MR on public GWAS suggested a positive genetic association of PM2.5 with PD; network toxicology intersected PM2.5-component targets, PD risk genes and differential transcripts (195 genes), and LASSO/RF picked INPP5D (SHIP1) as hub. Docking and SH-SY5Y experiments with SRM 1648a showed SHIP1 up-regulation, PI3K-AKT suppression, inflammation and apoptosis, rescued by INPP5D knockdown. Limitation: MR for an environmental exposure rests on GWAS of residential PM2.5, whose instruments mostly encode where people live (pleiotropy); docking affinities are not evidence. MR estimates are not reported in the abstract, nor is the SRM dose. Relevance: low.

PAPERS.short: Al-Atram early-life air pollution child neurodevelopment critical review 2026
PAPERS.title: Early Life Ambient Air Pollution and Child Neurodevelopment: Critical Review of Cohort Evidence
PAPERS.pm: Prenatal and early-childhood PM2.5, PM10, NO2
PAPERS.endpoint: Psychomotor, cognitive, behavioural outcomes; ASD/ADHD
PAPERS.n: Narrative critical review (purposive selection, PubMed through 30 Aug 2026) weighing null findings, exposure assessment, confounding and causal interpretation. European and US multicohort studies show small associations with selected outcomes alongside substantial nulls; Canadian and Korean cohorts show pollutant- and age-specific heterogeneity. Birth weight and prematurity require total vs conditional effect distinctions; placental and imaging data support plausibility but not mediation. The authors conclude the evidence does not make pollution a determinative cause of ASD or ADHD. Limitation: no protocol, duplicate screening or risk-of-bias scoring, so selection is the authors' own, and it predates today's Medicaid wildfire-ASD cohort. Relevance: low.

PAPERS.short: Awasthi air pollution oxidative stress inflammation molecular mechanisms review 2026
PAPERS.title: Molecular Mechanisms Linking Air Pollution-Induced Oxidative Stress to Inflammation and Human Disease
PAPERS.pm: PM, NOx, O3, SO2, VOCs (generic)
PAPERS.endpoint: Oxidative stress, inflammation, multi-system disease
PAPERS.n: Broad review of ROS/RNS generation by PM, NOx, O3, SO2 and VOCs and downstream Nrf2, NF-kB and MAPK signalling, mitochondrial dysfunction, ER stress and epigenetic reprogramming, mapped to respiratory, cardiovascular, neurological, metabolic and carcinogenic outcomes; also covers biomarkers, susceptible windows and antioxidant-based interventions. No quantitative synthesis. Limitation: pollutants with very different chemistry are pooled under one oxidative-stress narrative, and in vitro dose relevance is not appraised; nothing here is new relative to the established mechanistic literature. Relevance: low - background for oxidative-potential (OP) metrics, which are the measurable bridge to sensing.

PAPERS.short: Geng grain dust simulator manikin respirator workplace protection factor 2026
PAPERS.title: Using a Grain Dust Simulator with a Manikin System to Evaluate Performances of Commonly Used Respirators
PAPERS.pm: Respirable grain dust, 5-20 mg/m3; real-time on-farm grain-bin dust
PAPERS.endpoint: Simulated workplace protection factor (SWPF) of four respirators
PAPERS.n: A grain dust simulator combined with a breathing manikin estimated SWPFs for four common respiratory protection devices at four respirable dust levels (5, 10, 15, 20 mg/m3) and two inhalation flows (30 and 85 L/min), benchmarked against real-time dust in on-farm grain bins. The platform was repeatable and separated device performance; the nuisance dust mask is not recommended for grain bins. SWPF values are not in the abstract. Limitation: manikin faces do not reproduce human fit variability or movement, so SWPF overstates real protection for poorly fitted FFRs; a static simulator lacks the burst exposures of bin entry. Relevance: low-medium - inside/outside real-time dust monitors are the field version of this test.

PAPERS.short: Szalata waste fire toxic emissions Gaussian plume environmental risk 2026
PAPERS.title: Environmental Risk Assessment of Toxic Emissions into the Air Resulting from Waste Fires
PAPERS.pm: Modelled PM10, PM2.5 and gases from a waste-storage fire (Gaussian plume)
PAPERS.endpoint: Receptor concentrations vs Polish, EPA, OSHA and NDS reference values
PAPERS.n: Receptor-oriented screening: Gaussian plume (Pasquill classes) for a 14,000 kg municipal-waste fire burning 3.5 h, compared against Polish, US EPA, OSHA and NDS limits. Under the worst case analysed (class F, 1 m/s southerly) the residential receptor 700 m away stayed below reference values. Limitation: emission factors for mixed-waste fires are highly uncertain, and a steady-state Gaussian plume ignores fire-driven plume rise, lofting and near-field downwash, and comparing to occupational limits is not a public-health criterion. No measurement validates the field. Relevance: medium - rapid-deployment LCS around waste fires are the only practical check on such screening models.

PAPERS.short: Rosu multi-instrument Saharan dust event South-Eastern Europe 2026
PAPERS.title: A multi-instrument analysis of a Saharan dust event in South-Eastern Europe
PAPERS.pm: Saharan dust event (metadata only)
PAPERS.endpoint: Dust event characterisation
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: no abstract at Crossref, Europe PMC or Semantic Scholar on the issue date (Elsevier day-0 deposit). The title reports a multi-instrument analysis of a Saharan dust intrusion over South-Eastern Europe; instruments, sites, PM metrics and results are not available here and are not inferred. Limitation (structural): single-event case studies cannot establish event frequency or generalise dust contributions to PM10 exceedances. Relevance: medium - dust events are where optical LCS under-read coarse mass most strongly, so multi-instrument events are useful calibration benchmarks. Retry the abstract before the weekly; if PM10/PM2.5 ratios are reported, they matter for the coarse-mode LCS correction.

PAPERS.short: Saborit gas cooking indoor air quality households 7 European countries 2026
PAPERS.title: Characterization of the impact of gas cooking on indoor air quality in households across 7 European countries
PAPERS.pm: Household indoor air during gas cooking (metadata only)
PAPERS.endpoint: Indoor air quality impact of gas cooking
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: no abstract at Crossref, Europe PMC or Semantic Scholar on the issue date. The title reports household measurements of gas-cooking impacts on indoor air quality across seven European countries; which pollutants (NO2, PM2.5, ultrafine particles) were measured, the number of homes and the instrumentation are not available here and are not inferred. Limitation (structural): cooking PM is dominated by the food and method rather than the fuel, so attributing particle increments to gas requires an electric comparison arm. Relevance: medium - multi-country household campaigns of this type typically rely on low-cost PM and NO2 sensors. Retry the abstract before the weekly.
